<!-- docs/reference/events.md -->

# Events

`events(since=0)` returns the event list from the zero-based offset `since`; it must be an integer from zero through the current event count, inclusive. Use `next_since` from an advance result as the next offset. The driver stores `type` and driver-relative `tick` on every event. It does **not** add the `seq` required by the public `Event` TypedDict; `month` and `message` are optional in that type, not universal fields. TypedDicts describe responses and do not validate them.

| `type` | Additional fields and meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `lord_died` | The player's starting lord is no longer alive; emitted once when tracked. |
| `enemy_lord_died` | `player`: owner of a starting enemy lord, emitted once per lord. |
| `match_end` | `result` is `won` or `lost`. Mission events also have `game_over_flag`, `menu`, and `winners` (eight player flags); skirmish events instead have `winner` (1 on a win, otherwise a list of surviving enemy player IDs or `None`). |
| `month_end` | `month` (completed driver months), `gold`, `popularity`, `population`, `game_tick` (absolute game tick), `army`, `enemy_army`, `lord_alive`. AI games add `enemy_buildings` and `enemy_lords_alive`; missions with AI also add `enemy_lord_hp` (player IDs as string keys) and `lord_hp`. |
| `build_refused` | `building`, `x`, `y`; ordinary builds add `reason`, while wall lines add `tiles` and `built`. Detection occurs after time moves. |
| `demolish_refused` | `building_id` and `type` identify the building still present after time moves. Here `type` overwrites the event kind in the emitted dictionary: the actual returned `type` is the building type, not `demolish_refused`. |
| `order_stalled` | `cmd`, `ordered_at`, `units` (count), target fields (`x` and `y`, `target_id`, or `building_id`), `at` (first surviving unit's coordinates), and `note`. Mission order monitoring emits it when an order appears dropped. |

The watcher docstring also mentions siege arrival and defeat, but the current emission sites do not emit those events. `AdvanceResult` declares `tick`, `ticks_left`, `game_over`, `events`, and `next_since`; as in state, an unlimited budget can make `ticks_left` null despite its declared integer type.

<!-- docs/reference/goods.md -->

# Goods

The driver's stock snapshot uses the names and numeric good IDs below. Categories describe the driver's food slots and stores or weapons pages, not a guarantee of tradeability. Market prices and tradeable flags are read from the running game. Other uses are unknown unless listed.

| Good | ID | Driver category | Known use or source |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `wood` | 2 | stores page | unknown |
| `hops` | 3 | stores page | unknown |
| `stone` | 4 | stores page | unknown |
| `iron` | 6 | stores page | unknown |
| `pitch` | 7 | stores page | unknown |
| `wheat` | 9 | stores page | unknown |
| `bread` | 10 | food; granary | unknown |
| `cheese` | 11 | food; granary | unknown |
| `meat` | 12 | food; granary | unknown |
| `apples` | 13 | food; granary | unknown |
| `ale` | 14 | stores page | unknown |
| `gold` | 15 | currency | also exposed as `State.gold` |
| `flour` | 16 | stores page | unknown |
| `bows` | 17 | weapons page | fletcher product |
| `crossbows` | 18 | weapons page | fletcher product |
| `spears` | 19 | weapons page | poleturner product |
| `pikes` | 20 | weapons page | poleturner product |
| `maces` | 21 | weapons page | blacksmith product |
| `swords` | 22 | weapons page | blacksmith product |
| `leather_armor` | 23 | weapons page | unknown |
| `metal_armor` | 24 | weapons page | unknown |

Food is stored in the granary, weapons and armor in the armory, and other goods in the stockpile. Wheat is milled into flour and baked into bread; workers carry wood or iron to weapon workshops. The tanner uses dairy cows for leather armor.

<!-- docs/reference/map-legend.md -->

# Map legend

The driver's text map renders each tile using the first matching condition below:

| Character | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| space | Outside the valid tile area. |
| Building letter or `B` | A building occupies the tile; `B` is the fallback when its name has no mapped letter. |
| `~` | Tile lacks the land flag. |
| `f` | Farmland. |
| `^` | A blocked or wall tile. |
| `,` | Land with a farmable logic flag. |
| `.` | Other land. |

Building letters are `h` hovel, `w` woodcutter, `m` market, `c` chapel or church, `a` apple orchard, `d` dairy farm, `p` hunters post, `f` wheat farm, `n` mill, `k` bakery, `g` granary, `s` stockpile, `q` quarry, `b` brewery, `i` inn, `o` well, `j` hops farm, and `K` keep. Thus `f` is ambiguous between a wheat farm and farmland. The map character alone is not a complete building-placement test; the driver also checks units and other conditions.

`ascii_map(x0=0, y0=0, x1=399, y1=399)` returns newline-separated rows for an inclusive rectangle. Coordinates must be integers within the map, with lower bounds no greater than upper bounds. Building lookup happens before terrain checks, and `B` also covers unrecognized building names. This is a terrain/building display, not a unit display.

<!-- docs/reference/state.md -->

# State

`state()` returns visible game state. These TypedDicts describe responses; they do not validate them at runtime.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `tick`, `month` | Driver-relative elapsed ticks and completed months, respectively. |
| `ticks_per_month`, `ticks_left` | Month length (800 ticks) and remaining budget. `ticks_left` can be `None` with no budget despite its declared `int` type. |
| `game_over` | End reason or `None`. |
| `gold`, `stock` | Gold and named goods; gold also appears in `stock`. |
| `popularity`, `population`, `housing` | Current player values. |
| `tax`, `rations` | Tax is the raw value minus 3; rations is a name for recognized values, otherwise the raw number. |
| `date` | Game `month` and `year`, distinct from completed driver months. |
| `buildings` | Player-owned buildings, each with `id`, `type`, `x`, `y`. |
| `idle_peasants`, `units`, `lord_alive` | Idle peasant count, visible units and tracked player lord status. |

Each unit has `id`, `type`, `owner`, `x`, `y`, `hp`. At level 3 or higher, player-owned catapults and trebuchets include `ammo`; `cows` is included when positive. Missions exclude units with zero HP; non-missions may list them.

Mode-specific fields:

- `enemy` appears in AI games, with `lords` and `buildings`. Each enemy building has `id`, `type`, `x`, `y`, `owner`, `hp`, `max_hp`.
- `mission` appears when set.
- `allies` appears when allies exist: `players` is a sorted list of player IDs, `lords` is a list of lord records, and at level 6 or higher `panel` has one entry per ally. Each panel entry has `player`, `request` (`None` or `{good, qty}`), and `order` (`None`, `defend`, or `{attack: target}`).

Each enemy or ally lord record has `owner` and `alive`; a live lord additionally has `id`, `x`, `y`, `hp`. See [units](units.md) and [buildings](buildings.md).

`RawState` is a separate direct-memory snapshot: `tick` (absolute game tick), `paused`, `month`, `year`, `tax`, `rations`, `popularity`, `population`, `housing`, and `stock`. Tax and rations are raw, not normalized as in `State`.

<!-- docs/reference/units.md -->

# Units

A `Unit` has `id`, `type`, `owner`, `x`, `y` and `hp`; `ammo` and `cows` are optional. The driver reports recognized live unit types and excludes zero-health units in missions. A lord record has `owner` and `alive`; its `id`, position and health are optional.

Costs are per unit. European troop prices and equipment below were recorded in the supplied import reference; the driver reads them from the running game, which is authoritative. Recruits require an idle peasant. Roles below list only capabilities explicitly identified in the driver, not a complete combat description. Availability and command acceptance depend on game state and driver level.

| Unit | Cost | Recruitment building | Known role or action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `archer` | 12 gold, bow | `barracks` | can dig moat; can light pitch; ranged; attack ground |
| `crossbowman` | 20 gold, crossbow, leather armor | `barracks` | ranged; attack ground |
| `spearman` | 8 gold, spear | `barracks` | can dig moat |
| `pikeman` | 20 gold, pike, metal armor | `barracks` | can dig moat |
| `maceman` | 20 gold, mace, leather armor | `barracks` | can dig moat |
| `swordsman` | 40 gold, sword, metal armor | `barracks` | unknown |
| `knight` | 40 gold, sword, metal armor; horse at level 2+ | `barracks` | unknown |
| `arabian_archer` | 75 gold | `mercenary_post` | can light pitch; ranged; attack ground |
| `slave` | 5 gold | `mercenary_post` | can dig moat |
| `slinger` | 12 gold | `mercenary_post` | ranged; attack ground |
| `assassin` | 60 gold | `mercenary_post` | unknown |
| `horse_archer` | 80 gold | `mercenary_post` | ranged; attack ground |
| `arabian_swordsman` | 80 gold | `mercenary_post` | unknown |
| `fire_thrower` | 100 gold | `mercenary_post` | ranged; attack ground |
| `engineer` | 30 gold | `engineers_guild` | can dig moat; can operate oil smelter |
| `laddermen` | 4 gold | `engineers_guild` | raise ladders against enemy walls |
| `tunneler` | 30 gold | `tunnelers_guild` | dig tunnel toward enemy wall or building |
| `monk` | 10 gold | `cathedral` | unknown |
| `lord` | unknown | `unknown` | unknown |

The driver also names siege engines when enabled. The table does not establish their recruitment costs or buildings.
